title: 257. why you can be loved and still feel unlovable (feat. dr. marisa franco)
description_html: why do some people struggle to accept love?? today’s guest is dr. marisa g. franco— a psychologist, author, professor, and friendship expert. she writes about how to build relationships with yourself and others for psychology today and has been a featured connection expert for major publications like the new york times, the telegraph, and vice.
talk_about: how self-worth and relationships are tied together
how you can be loved but not feel loved
how memories become the database of your self-worth
how to rewrite the memories that shaped you
supporting someone who can't accept your love
how i found 1% of hope in recovery
what we get wrong about attachment styles
the one thing to take away from this episode

guests: dr. marisa g. franco, psychologist, author, professor, and friendship expert
summary: sadie and dr. marisa g. franco explore why people can be surrounded by love and still feel unworthy of it. they discuss how low self-worth acts as a filter that blocks out compliments and affection, why positive feedback can actually feel threatening when it conflicts with your self-image, and how past memories form a database that predicts future harm. dr. franco explains memory reconsolidation—a research-backed way to emotionally rewrite formative memories—and why meeting yourself where you are (not forcing positivity) is the foundation of healing. listeners learn practical tools for building self-worth internally and supporting loved ones who struggle to accept care.
quote: it's not that people with low self-esteem don't wanna be loved, it's just that they feel misunderstood, and we need to feel understood to feel loved.
quote_display: it's not that people with low self-esteem don't wanna be LOVED, it's just that they feel MISUNDERSTOOD, and we need to feel UNDERSTOOD to feel LOVED.
